30 Two cylindrical conductors, X and Y, are made from the same material. The conductors have
equal lengths, but Y has a smaller diameter than X.
X and Y are connected in series to a cell.
Which row compares the number of charge carriers per unit time passing through X and through
Y and compares the average drift speed of the charge carriers in X and in Y?
average drift speed
number of charge
carriers per unit time
of charge carriers
A
Y greater than X
Y greater than X
B
Y same as X
Y same as X
C
Y greater than X
Y same as X
D
Y same as X
Y greater than X

hints: Notice that X and Y are connected in series to the cell, so ask what is identical for the two conductors - the current $I$.
Connect current to the first column using charge per carrier: number per unit time $= I/q$, where $q$ is the electron charge.
Connect current to the second column using $I = nAvq$, with the same $n$ for the same material but smaller cross-sectional area $A$ for the smaller-diameter conductor Y.
walkthrough: In series the same current $I$ flows through X and through Y, because charge cannot accumulate at the junction.
The number of carriers passing per unit time is $I/q$, where $q$ is the charge on one carrier, so equal $I$ means Y same as X for this column.
Use $I = nAvq$ for drift speed $v$, where $n$ is number density of carriers and $A$ is cross-sectional area.
X and Y are the same material so $n$ and $q$ are the same, and equal lengths do not affect this equation, but Y has smaller diameter so $A_Y < A_X$.
With $I$, $n$ and $q$ fixed, $v = I/(nAq)$ must be larger when $A$ is smaller, so the average drift speed in Y is greater than in X.
Same carriers per unit time with greater drift speed in Y matches the row with Y same as X and Y greater than X. This is option D.

A.explanation: Current is the same in series, so carriers per unit time cannot be greater in Y, although drift speed is greater in Y.

B.explanation: Carriers per unit time are the same, but drift speed cannot be the same because Y has smaller cross-sectional area with the same current.

C.explanation: Drift speed is not the same and carriers per unit time are not greater in Y; series connection forces the same current in X and Y.

D.explanation: Same current gives same carriers per unit time, and smaller area in Y requires larger drift speed from $I = nAvq$.
